fatal_errors: The proposed intervention varies Al content and multiple annealing variables rather than testing the fixed Cr39Co18Fe18Ni18Al7 alloy annealed at 1100–1300 °C and water-quenched.
The central mechanism—cooling-induced spinodal separation into Ni–Al-lean BCC and Ni–Al-rich BCC, followed by B2 ordering and reciprocal hierarchical BCC/B2 decomposition—is absent.
The stated 500–1000 °C boundary excludes the target annealing range.
The yield-strength, fracture-toughness, and percentage-improvement predictions and baseline values are invented and do not correspond to the reported hardness comparison.
The falsification rule tests arbitrary mechanical-property thresholds rather than whether phase stability is governed by spinodal decomposition and Ni–Al ordering.
The cited evidence concerns other HEA systems or broad HEA behavior and does not support the specific Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni mechanism.
explanation: The response only captures the broad idea that composition and heat treatment influence FCC/BCC balance. It misses the fixed alloy, controlled anneal-and-quench temperature series, B2 ordering, reciprocal elemental partitioning, sequential spinodal-decomposition hypothesis, and monotonic hardness increase from approximately 39 to 50 HRC. Its experiment changes composition and processing simultaneously, weakening causal discrimination, while its falsification criterion is disconnected from the claimed phase-stability mechanism. The numerical mechanical-property baseline and predicted gains have no support in the supplied evidence, and the citations do not validate the proposed mechanism.
